subject: Trial readiness & metrics handshake
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@novalytics.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@novalytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Trial readiness & metrics handshake

Hi Elena / Carlos,

Great to connect earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff: 

1) Trial objective (what success looks like)
   - Technical: 95th percentile generation latency <= 200ms for our common prompt set (avg prompt length ~120 tokens) under a 30 RPS sustained workload.
   - Throughput: capability to handle 50 concurrent inference requests with <250ms p95 latency.
   - Cost: target gross cost <= $0.0025 per token for productionized config (we'll show tradeoffs between quantized and full precision).
   - Quality: top-line quality target is >= 87% pass rate on your labeled prompt set (we'll run a blind eval using your rubric).

2) Evaluation plan / instrumentation
   - We'll run a 2-week POC: 3-day smoke, 10-day controlled evaluation, 4-day soak/edge cases.
   - Artifacts we need from you: 1) evaluation prompt set (representative prompts + expected outputs), 2) labeled quality rubric, 3) sample traffic shape (RPS distribution).
   - Measurement: Redwood will provide token-level cost reporting, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and end-to-end success metrics (accuracy/QA pass). Marcus (cc'd) will own the instrumentation and smoke test.

3) Ownership and timeline
   - Redwood owners: Ben (engagement lead), Marcus (SE / instrumentation), Lauren (customer success / billing).
   - Novalytics owners: Elena (product), Carlos (infra).
   - Proposed kickoff: week of Jul 19; smoke test Jul 20-22; controlled eval Jul 23-Aug 2.

4) Open questions / constraints from your side
   - Any regulatory retention or audit logging window we should be aware of?
   - Do you need a private deployment (VPC) for the trial or is hosted API acceptable?

Action items: please confirm the metric targets above (latency/throughput/cost/quality), upload the eval prompt set, and confirm availability for the Jul 19 kickoff. If anything here looks off, reply with edits and we’ll revise.

Attachments: redwood-poc-template.xlsx (POC milestones + roles), eval-prompt-set.md (sample format).

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

---

From: Elena Park <elena@novalytics.com>

Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@novalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial readiness & metrics handshake

Hi Ben — thanks for the summary, this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The quality rubric is the most important metric for the product team; the 87% pass target seems reasonable but can you confirm how you compute "pass rate" (exact match, token-level BLEU-ish, or human review)?
- For latency: our production SLA target is p95 < 150ms, but we can be flexible for the POC if you can show a clear path to 150ms in production.
- We will need audit logs retained for 90 days for the trial (preferred) — can you confirm retention and exportability?
- Hosted API is fine for the controlled eval; we may request a VPC for final proof if we move to Dedicated.

I uploaded an initial prompt set (redacted) to the Drive folder and added expected outputs for 120 prompts. Carlos will follow up with a traffic sample.

Can we tentatively commit to Jul 20 smoke test? That gives our infra team time to whitelist Redwood IP ranges.

Best,
Elena
Head of Product | Novalytics
elena@novalytics.com

Thanks Elena — great notes. A few specific answers and tweaks below: 

- Quality pass definition: we'll run automated checks first (string similarity and a task-specific heuristic you provide) and surface a stratified sample to your reviewers for blind human scoring. The "pass rate" reported in the POC dashboard will be the human-reviewed pass proportion; automated heuristics will be reported separately.
- Latency path: we will instrument p95 at both the request gateway (end-to-end) and the model runtime (intra-GPU). For the POC we'll show both; production optimizations (dedicated pools + kernel tuning) are how we get to ~150ms p95.
- Audit logs: Redwood hosted API retains request/response metadata for 90 days by default and exports as compressed JSON; we'll share a sample export during the smoke test.

Next steps I will take today:
- Share the redwood-poc-template.xlsx with milestone owners filled (attached).
- Provide a short eval prompt format example (eval-prompt-set.md) — see attachments.
- Confirm smoke test window Jul 20-22.

If Jul 20 works, Marcus will send a short pre-smoke checklist for your infra (IP allowlists, API keys, sample payloads).

Ben

Hi all — Marcus (SE) here. Quick tech notes to make sure evaluation measurements are reproducible: 

- Latency measurement: we'll report both client-observed E2E p95 (includes network) and server-side model-step p95 (excludes gateway). For fairness, please share whether your sample traffic includes any complex transforms pre-call.
- Throughput tests: our load harness uses token-accurate replay; please identify any dynamic prompt expansion rules so we can simulate realistic token growth.
- Cost/token: our cost calc will include tokenized input + output + fixed per-request overhead; if you have an estimated average response length for the 120 prompts, please add that to the Drive doc.

I'll set up a staging endpoint for Jul 20 smoke runs and share the endpoint + basic runbook. Attaching a short smoke-test checklist below.

Attachment: smoke-test-checklist.md (instrumentation steps + command snippets)

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
